rows.summary: Each opening of Auto-Generate reads the letter's own Recipient Name and Company (a letter with no name is greeted "Dear Hiring Team,", no more "Hiring Manager" default), so a typed recipient and the title typed for them survive Apply and the body names the company the block prints; Apply writes the company whole, so a blank generator Company clears the old one. Product call: the Target Role is not prefilled (the letter stores no role, only a subject).

The job-description scanner keeps an apostrophe (straight or curly) inside its word: "You'll", "we're", "don't" are the stop words they are, any other contraction is dropped, "Stripe's" reads as "Stripe" and "O'Reilly" stays whole; the résumé corpus reads curly apostrophes as straight too.

The pasted job description is kept for the browser tab's session (sessionStorage, key cpwtcv_ats_jd:<résumé id>, via useSessionState) and the ATS panel is keyed by the résumé id, so the posting and its Match % survive a trip to another tab, and another résumé's scanner starts empty.

rows.summary: /\b(did)\b/ cannot match inside "didn't": there is no word boundary between "did" and "n", so Auto-Fix never wrote "deliveredn't". A lookahead fix (5f99091) was proven unnecessary by failfirst (its test passed without it) and reverted (78582e9); the test stays as a guard. Reviewer B checked every weak phrase: none can precede an apostrophe in realistic text.

With "Group roles by company" on, printedJobs tags each later role of a group with its first role (groupLead), and jobFields gives it that role's company outcome, and its location outcome where the location is the shared one the employer header prints; a role's own differing location is read under it, and a grouped role with no title is read just after the role before it.

A power verb chip replaces a leading action verb, a multi-word verb phrase Auto-Fix writes ("Contributed to") or a leading weak phrase ("Responsible for" → "Spearheaded"); otherwise it goes before the first word, lowercased when it is an ordinary capitalised word ("AWS" stays). Line breaks, bullet marks and quotes are kept (insertActionVerb in bulletOptimizer.js).
rows.remaining: A proper noun leading the statement ("Kubernetes cluster…") is lowercased when the verb is prepended (low).

rows.summary: A metric chip goes before the statement's closing punctuation ("…checkout service by 35%."), and on an empty statement it is the phrase alone, no leading space (insertMetric).
rows.remaining: A statement ending in an abbreviation's dot ("etc.") loses it before the metric (low).

rows.summary: hasMetric (the optimizer's and the ATS score's one rule) reads calendar years, decades, year ranges and month/year dates ("in 2021", "the 1990s", "2019–22", "05/2021") as no number; "2000+", "$2019", "2019%" and "2020k" still count.
rows.remaining: A bare count that looks like a year ("Served 2000 users") now reads as no metric — the trade-off of the finding's own rule. "FY2021" still counts (pre-existing: the digit rule checks only the first digit).

rows.summary: extractBulletsFromItem reads a list description through parseRichText, as the PDF prints it: every list item, nested or not, is its own bullet, and an item's continuation paragraph stays with it.
rows.remaining: Text after a nested list inside the same outer item joins the nested bullet, not the outer one (low, count unchanged).

rows.summary: needsAtsTitle also asks for a shown entry on the résumé's template, the rule has_exp/has_edu/has_skills use, so an empty or all-hidden section is neither flagged as a non-standard heading nor renamed by Standardize Headings (the panel passes resume.template).
